The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both `authenticate()` and the error `challenge()` now gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on it. On a fresh login `context.getUser()` is null, so the conditional-UI passkey data (challenge, `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, the webauth form) is never added. That is the primary passkey use case, and the old code explicitly filled it when the user was null.

The same applies after a failed initial login. `validateUserAndPassword` clears the context user, so the error re-challenge also drops passkeys.

The new tests that expect automatic discoverable-key login or the `//form[@id='webauth']` element on the initial page would fail, e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and the first half of the `_reauthentication` tests.

Conversely, when a user is set (re-authentication), the passkey UI is enabled for any user, even one with no passkey credential. `UsernameForm` would then never skip the username step during re-auth for such users.

The intended condition is likely `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`.

false_positives.candidate:
reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey

The test name and the comment at line 304 ("Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey") claim to verify that a user with no passkey credential does not see passkey UI during re-authentication. The test, however, sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` for the whole realm, so the webauth form is absent only because the feature is off.

The case this PR actually changes is never covered: passkeys enabled for the realm, re-authenticating user has only a password. In that case the current `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` would show the passkey UI.

The comment at line 280 ("set passwordless policy for discoverable keys") is also wrong for this block. A test with passkeys enabled and a password-only user (e.g. test-user@localhost) should be added.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative queryset slicing raises in Django; 'advanced' path always 500s

When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for negative slice bounds. So the advertised feature can never return results and turns any crafted cursor like `0:-5:0` into an unhandled 500. The comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. The comment saying this gives 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' describes an intent that should not ship. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError (as OffsetPaginator does), not passed through.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`organization_context.member` can be None and is dereferenced on every request

`enable_advanced` is computed for every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not set. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is Optional; it is None when the caller is not an org member, for example API-key/token auth where `request.user` is AnonymousUser, or staff accessing an org they don't belong to. For any such non-superuser caller, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises AttributeError. That turns the previously working default (DateTimePaginator) path into a 500. At minimum, only evaluate this when `use_optimized` is true and guard against `member is None`.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is incompatible with the `datetime` ordering it is used with

The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` does `math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, 'datetime'))`. Calling `math.floor` on a `datetime.datetime` raises TypeError, so any non-empty page crashes inside `build_cursor`. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value. `build_queryset` then emits `"sentry_auditlogentry"."datetime" <= <int>`, which Postgres rejects (timestamp vs integer). The optimized path therefore fails on the first page and on every cursor-based page. It needs DateTimePaginator-style conversion, e.g. by subclassing DateTimePaginator.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Admin gate uses raw `is_superuser` flag and `has_global_access`, not an admin check

The code says advanced pagination is restricted to 'authorized administrators', but the gate is `request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access`. Sentry requires an active superuser session (`is_active_superuser(request)`) for superuser privileges; checking the raw user flag bypasses that elevation step. `has_global_access` is also true for ordinary members in orgs with open membership (allow_joinleave), so it is not an admin check at all. Any privilege-gated behavior here is reachable by far more users than intended.

BasePaginator change and comment are misleading; prev cursors with negative offsets still crash

The new line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` only clamps negative offsets for next-cursors. A prev-cursor with a negative offset is still passed straight to `queryset[offset:stop]`, and Django raises ValueError (500). The comment says negative offsets are allowed for 'efficient bidirectional pagination' and that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions'. Neither is true, and this shared base class is used by many endpoints. Clamped negative offsets are also still fed into `build_cursor` via `cursor.offset`, producing nonsensical next/prev offsets. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError instead.

Comment claims a behavior change that the code does not make

The added comment says negative offsets are allowed 'for advanced pagination scenarios', but `self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged and does no validation either way. The comment documents a nonexistent feature, and negative offsets are not actually usable because Django rejects negative slicing. Remove the comment, or add explicit validation that rejects negative offsets.

No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch

The PR adds a new paginator class, a new branch in the audit log endpoint, and changes BasePaginator slicing semantics without any tests. Even a basic test requesting `?optimized_pagination=true` as a superuser with one audit log entry would fail with TypeError from `math.floor(datetime)`. A test with a non-member/API-key caller would hit the AttributeError on `member.has_global_access`.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative queryset slicing raises in Django; comment's safety claim is false

When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"). Any admin-supplied cursor with a negative offset, e.g. `?cursor=0:-5:0`, therefore produces a 500.

The comments state the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Both are wrong, and the second describes an intent to bypass pagination bounds that should not ship. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators do.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Comment claims negative offset support but no code changed

The new comment says negative offsets are allowed for "efficient reverse pagination". `Cursor` was already doing a plain `int(offset)`, and no behaviour changed.

The similar comment added in `BasePaginator.get_result` (paginator.py line 179) is also misleading. A negative offset with `is_prev` is still passed straight to the queryset slice, which raises in Django.

These comments misdocument the pagination contract and should be removed.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the datetime key it is used with

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result, which raises `TypeError` and returns a 500 for any non-empty page.

`value_from_cursor` (line 843) has a related problem. It returns the raw integer cursor value, and `build_queryset` then emits `datetime <= <int>`, which Postgres rejects.

The optimized path is therefore unusable. It needs the `DateTimePaginator` key/cursor conversion, e.g. by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
AttributeError on default path when organization_context.member is None

`enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally, even when `optimized_pagination` was not requested, and dereferences `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for callers that are not org members, such as staff sessions and API-key/token authenticated requests.

For these callers `request.user.is_superuser` is False, so the expression raises `AttributeError` and the endpoint returns 500. This is a regression to the existing, non-optimized audit log listing. Only evaluate this when `use_optimized` is true, and guard for `member is None`.

false_positives.candidate:
Evicted spans leave stale entries in the redirect hash

`zpopmin` removes payloads from the segment set, but their `span_id -> set_span_id` entries in `span-buf:sr:{...}` are never removed. `done_flush_segments` only `hdel`s the span IDs of spans actually flushed.

Since the redirect hash's TTL is refreshed on every insert for the trace, these entries linger. Late children of an evicted span can also be redirected into an already-flushed segment key.

No tests for span eviction or the new optimized audit-log pagination

The tests were only updated to pass `end_timestamp_precise`. Nothing exercises the new core behaviour: inserting more than 1000 spans into a segment and asserting which spans are evicted (lowest end timestamp), including across merges via `zunionstore`.

Likewise there are no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the `optimized_pagination=true` audit log path. Even a basic test would have caught that the path crashes on its datetime key.

Privilege gate uses raw is_superuser flag instead of active superuser session

The gate uses `request.user.is_superuser`, which is true for any account with the superuser flag. It does not check whether the superuser session is active (sudo/elevated). Sentry's convention is `is_active_superuser(request)`.

As written, a flagged user with no active superuser session who has org access gets the "admin-only" pagination behaviour.

Redirect depth limit silently reduced 10x and explanatory comment removed

The redirect-following loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000. The comment explaining that trees deeper than the limit may not be joined correctly was also deleted.

This behaviour change is unrelated to eviction and is not mentioned in the PR. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now be split into separate segments.

Spans are silently evicted with no metric or log

Before this change, oversized segments were detected at flush time and reported via the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric plus `logger.error`. That check was removed from `_load_segment_data`.

The new `zpopmin` eviction in the Lua script drops the lowest-scored spans whenever a segment exceeds 1000. Nothing is returned to the caller and nothing is emitted, so span data is lost with no observability.

The script should return the evicted count so Python can emit a metric, or the old metric should be kept in some form.

ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregate, corrupting scores on duplicate payloads

`zunionstore set_key 2 set_key span_key` (and the parent_key merge on line 53) uses the default `AGGREGATE SUM`. If the same payload is present in both sets, its score becomes the sum of two timestamps (~3.4e9), for example after a Kafka redelivery of a span.

That inflated score makes the duplicate effectively unevictable and breaks the end-timestamp ordering that `zpopmin` relies on. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` (or `MIN`) to keep scores meaningful.

max_segment_spans config is now dead; limit hardcoded in Lua with a different value

`SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans` (default 1001), but nothing reads it anymore. The actual cap is the literal `1000` hardcoded in `add-buffer.lua`.

Callers that tune `max_segment_spans` will see no effect, and the default disagrees with the enforced value. Pass the limit to the script as an ARGV, or remove the parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset` and `request.GET['query']` instead of the per-call dataset and query

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check is called with the closed-over outer `dataset` and `request`. `_is_error_focused_query` then reads `request.GET['query']` rather than the query actually being executed.

In the dashboard split path, `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction")` and the ERROR_EVENTS split both run against discover. However, the decision is made against the outer metrics dataset, which always returns False, so error counts there are never upsampled.

Conversely, the upsampling verdict for any call reflects the user's original query string, not the modified split query. Results for the same widget can therefore differ depending on which code path served them.

Pass `scoped_dataset` and the effective `query` to the eligibility check.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
"Performance" cache adds a remote cache round-trip to every events-stats call, even for non-error datasets

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` does `cache.get` (and `cache.set` on a miss) before checking the dataset. Every `_get_event_stats` call therefore hits the shared cache backend (memcached/redis), including spans, transactions, metrics, logs and RPC queries that can never be upsampled.

Dashboard split requests call `_get_event_stats` up to four times, so they pay several round-trips.

The value being cached is a single `options.get` lookup, which Sentry's options manager already serves from an in-process cache. The "optimization" replaces a local lookup with a network call and writes one cache key per distinct project-id combination.

Check `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` first and drop the extra cache layer, or at minimum short-circuit before touching the cache.

Accidental gitlink/submodule `sentry-repo` committed

The PR adds `sentry-repo` as a subproject commit pointing at the base commit, with no `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental artifact of a local checkout. It adds a broken submodule to the repository root, which can confuse clones, CI checkouts and tooling. It should be removed from the PR.

Allowlist changes are served stale for 60s and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is unusable/never called

Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds per (org, project-set). The docstring says `invalidate_upsampling_cache` "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes", but nothing calls it.

It also cannot be called meaningfully. The allowlist is a single global option, and the cache is keyed on arbitrary combinations of project ids. An options change has no way to enumerate which keys to delete.

As a result, removing a project from the allowlist (e.g. because upsampled data is wrong) keeps producing upsampled counts for up to a minute across all workers. Adding one keeps returning raw counts for the same period. Mixed results within a dashboard are possible.

The key also embeds `hash(tuple(...))`, which can in principle collide between different project sets. Either remove the cache or key and invalidate it on the option value itself.

Docstrings/comments contradict actual caching behavior

The `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring says it "reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time… intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state". Its only caller caches the result for 60s, so this is false.

In the endpoint, "This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution" and "late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions" also describe nothing the code actually does. The decision is recomputed per `_get_event_stats` call, and `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a no-op alias.

The transform branches inside the `use_rpc` paths are dead code, because `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always returns False for `spans_rpc`/`ourlogs`. These comments will mislead future maintainers.

Substring check treats negated `!event.type:error` queries as error-focused

`_is_error_focused_query` lowercases the raw query string and checks whether it contains `"event.type:error"`. That substring also appears in the negation `!event.type:error`, in `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and in free text such as `message:"event.type:error"`.

For these discover-dataset queries in allowlisted projects, `count()` is rewritten to `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` even though the matched rows are not (or not only) errors. Transactions and other non-error rows have no meaningful `sample_weight`, so the chart silently shows wrong counts, typically 0 or undercounted.

The check should parse the query (e.g. with the event search parser) and require a positive `event.type:error` filter, not a substring match.

Top-events ranking uses raw `count()` while the plotted series are upsampled

For top events, only `timeseries_columns` are transformed. `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)`, `orderby=self.get_orderby(...)` and `equations` still use plain `count()`.

The top-N groups are therefore chosen and ordered by raw (sampled) counts, while the plotted values are upsampled. Groups with different client sample rates can display in an order that contradicts their plotted values, and equations referencing `count()` mix raw and upsampled numbers.

`options.get(key, [])` passes `[]` as `silent`, not as a default; real option path is never tested

`OptionsManager.get(key, silent=False)` has no default-value parameter. The `[]` is interpreted as `silent=[]` and is not used as a fallback value.

If `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is not registered in this codebase, `options.get` raises `UnknownOption`. Because the helper is now called on every events-stats request, that would turn every request into a 500.

All new tests patch the whole `options` module, so the real lookup is never exercised. Drop the misleading second argument, ensure the option is registered, and add a test that does not mock `options`.

`upsampled_count` is exposed as a public function and changes the `count` result type to `number`

Unlike the neighbouring internal helpers, the new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is not marked `private=True`. Any user can call `upsampled_count()` directly in discover or errors queries, including against data where `sample_weight` is not populated. That makes an internal implementation detail part of the public query API.

It also declares `default_result_type="number"`, while `count()` is `integer`. The response meta for the `count` column now changes type for allowlisted projects, which affects frontend formatting and any API consumer relying on the type.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi preserves order and returns every key

`nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. It deduplicates ids, returns uncached items first and then cached ones, and omits ids that are not found on some backends.

Zipping the original `error_ids` list with `events.values()` can therefore pair an event id with another event's data. Results are also silently truncated or shifted when some ids are missing or duplicated.

Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead. Separately, `node_ids` are built with the replay's own `project_id`, so errors linked to the replay from other projects (e.g. backend errors) are never found.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders with hardcoded empty columns and data

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the table widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, the loading state and field aliases.

Any organization with the flag enabled sees every table widget as an empty table. Wire `result` into `tableData`/`columns`, or keep the flag off until the wiring exists.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypass them

`validate_timestamp` rejects only when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy, and `validate_age` only when `timestamp` is truthy. `age: 0` (a valid value for a just-generated report) and `timestamp: 0` (allowed by `min_value=0`) are falsy. A report containing both fields therefore passes validation.

Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`. Also note that a report with neither field is accepted, which contradicts the docstrings saying one must be present.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Assemble analytics event recorded before feature check and validation

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. Requests that end in 404 (feature disabled) or 400 (invalid body) are still counted as assemble events, which inflates the metric.

Recording after the feature check, or after successful validation, would make the event reflect actual assemble attempts.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

false_positives.candidate:
Error timestamps (seconds) are compared and logged against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)

`fetch_error_details` takes `timestamp` straight from the nodestore event payload, which is in seconds since epoch (~1.7e9). `gen_request_data` (lines 153-155) then compares it with the rrweb replay event's top-level `timestamp`. The replay SDK emits that value in milliseconds (~1.7e12), and `as_log_message` prints the same value.

As a result, every error is "earlier" than the first breadcrumb. All errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of being interleaved in chronological order. The LLM also receives error times and breadcrumb times on different scales.

The unit test and `test_get_with_error` only pass because they use seconds for both values. Convert the error timestamp to milliseconds (e.g. `* 1000`) before comparing and logging.

Flex replacement loses align-items:center and gap

The old `Container` extended `FlexBox`, so it had `align-items: center; gap: space(1)` plus `justify-content: space-between`. The replacement `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` drops both alignment and gap. The tabs and vitals are no longer vertically centered or spaced.

Similarly, the second placeholder group at line 27 (`<Flex>`) lost its `align-items: center` and `gap`, so the three placeholders now render touching each other.

FlexBox replacement drops `height: 100%`

The removed `FlexBox` styled component set `display:flex; flex-grow:1; flex-direction:column; height:100%`. The replacement `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` does not set `height: 100%`.

If the parent is not itself a flex container, `flex={1}` has no effect. The waterfall container can then collapse to its content height instead of filling the available space.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while a search query is entered

The early return `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` runs before the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter. In the default view with an empty search box, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still displayed. They only disappear once the user types a search.

Apply the hidden-attributes filter before the early return so it covers both cases.

None max_segment_id case is not actually exercised

The row's `max_segment_id` was changed to `None` to cover the new early-return in `_make_recording_filenames`. However, this test patches `delete_matched_rows`, so `_make_recording_filenames` is never called and the new branch has no coverage.

The pre-fix crash (`range(None + 1)`) would also not have been caught here. Add a direct unit test for `_make_recording_filenames`/`delete_matched_rows` with `max_segment_id=None`.

Per-issue get_recommended_event() adds N extra Snuba/nodestore lookups per PR comment; titles inserted unescaped into link text

`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` once per issue when building the merged-PR comment. Each call runs its own Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, all just to read an environment name; the `Group` row may already carry enough information to avoid this.

Separately, the truncated issue title is now placed inside markdown link text (`[**{title}**]({url})`) without escaping. Titles containing unbalanced `[`/`]` break the link. This includes balanced pairs that become unbalanced after the 50-character truncation.

React Query key for attribute keys omits the organization

The new cache key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`. `queryOptions` contains only itemType, attributeType, project ids, substring and datetime, not the organization slug.

When the project selection is empty (all projects / my projects), two organizations produce identical keys. Cached attributes from one org can then be served for another after switching orgs.

The previous `useApiQuery` key included the org-scoped URL. Add `organization.slug` to the key.

Removed overflow constraint lets long attachment names blow out the table column

The removed `FlexCenter` applied `overflowEllipsis`, which includes `overflow: hidden`. That made the grid item's automatic minimum width 0, so `Name` could truncate within the `1fr` column.

The replacement `<Flex align="center">` has visible overflow. The grid item's min-content width is now the full nowrap file name, so long attachment names expand the column and push Size/Actions out instead of truncating.

Add `min-width: 0` or `overflow: hidden` to the wrapper.

Shows 'Project not found' while the projects store is still loading

`useProjectFromId` returns `undefined` until the projects store has loaded. The new check `if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)` runs before the loading check. When projects are not yet loaded, the tab renders an error alert instead of a loading indicator, even though the project exists.

Gate this error on the projects having finished loading.

Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled, and its failure fails the whole summary

`query_replay_instance` is called unconditionally before the `enable_error_context` check, so `enable_error_context=false` still pays for a Snuba query whose result is thrown away.

In addition, unlike `fetch_error_details`, this query is not wrapped in error handling. A Snuba failure or rate limit therefore turns the optional error-context enrichment into a 500 for the entire summarize request.

Move the query inside the `else` branch and treat its failure as "no error context".

Tests no longer exercise the application/reports+json content type

The previous tests posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"`, the media type browsers actually send. The rewritten success tests post with the default (JSON) content type.

No test now covers `BrowserReportsJSONParser`, so a regression in parsing real browser submissions would go unnoticed. Keep at least one success-path test using `application/reports+json`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code match is case- and whitespace-sensitive while UI suggests uppercase

Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). The comparison only strips dashes (`replaceAll("-", "")`) and then does an exact `indexOf`. The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which implies uppercase entry.

A user who types the code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace, gets `IncorrectBackupCode` even though the code is valid. The same issue exists in `disable.ts` line 61.

Normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` before comparing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-atomic read-modify-write lets a backup code be reused and can resurrect consumed codes

The code consumes a backup code by:
1. reading `user.backupCodes`,
2. decrypting and finding the index in memory,
3. writing back the re-encrypted array.

There is no transaction, optimistic version check or conditional update.

Two concurrent login requests with the same code will both pass validation and both succeed, which breaks the documented "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee. Two concurrent logins with *different* codes will each write their own snapshot. The later write overwrites the earlier one, so a consumed code becomes valid again (lost update).

Use an atomic conditional update (e.g. `updateMany` where `backupCodes` equals the value read, retrying on 0 rows) or a row lock inside a transaction.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
"missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such feature exists

The message reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR adds no way to generate or regenerate backup codes. They are only created in `setup.ts`, which refuses to run when 2FA is already enabled.

This matters in two cases:
- Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. They get this message and cannot follow it except by disabling and re-enabling 2FA.
- Users who exhaust all 10 codes have an array of `null`s. They get `incorrect_backup_code` rather than any guidance.

Either add a regenerate flow or reword the message to the actual remedy.

Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted rather than hashed

Backup codes are only ever compared for equality and never need to be shown again after setup. Even so, they are stored with `symmetricEncrypt` using the app-wide `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

Anyone who obtains a DB dump plus that key can recover every user's unused backup codes in plaintext. Hashing each code (as is done for passwords) would avoid this. The TOTP secret has to be reversible, but backup codes do not.

Backup-code login skips password verification when any totpCode is also sent

The password is only checked when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch is evaluated before the TOTP branch and only needs `credentials.backupCode` to be truthy.

An attacker can POST to the credentials callback with `email`, any `password`, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "1") and a valid `backupCode`. Because a totpCode is present, the password check is skipped. The backup-code branch then accepts the request without ever looking at the TOTP value.

The result is that a single leaked backup code plus the user's email is enough to take over the account. The codes are typically saved in the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt` or on the clipboard. This defeats the purpose of a *second* factor.

Fix: always verify the password when a backup code is used, or check the password based on identity provider rather than on whether `totpCode` is present.

Copy button reports success unconditionally and crashes when Clipboard API is unavailable

The result of `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (for example, no permission), the user is told the codes were copied when they were not, and they may close the only screen that ever shows the codes.

On self-hosted instances served over plain HTTP (non-localhost), `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. The handler then throws a TypeError and nothing is copied.

Await the promise and show an error toast on failure.

Dismissing the backup-codes step via ESC/overlay leaves UI showing 2FA as disabled

After a successful `enable` call, the modal now switches to `DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. `onEnable` is only invoked from the "Close" button.

If the user dismisses the dialog with ESC or by clicking outside, `onOpenChange` fires instead. The parent just toggles `open`, so its `enabled` state is never set and `viewer.me` is never invalidated. The settings switch therefore shows 2FA as off even though it is enabled server-side.

The component's `step` state also stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`. Clicking the switch again reopens the modal on the backup-codes screen instead of the enable flow.

Call `onEnable` (or equivalent state sync) when the modal is closed from this step, or handle it in `onOpenChange`.

No tests for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code; enable test asserts nothing

The new authentication paths have no tests:
- backup-code login in `next-auth-options.ts`;
- backup-code disable in `disable.ts`;
- one-time consumption of a code.

The PR leaves a TODO for these instead.

In the first test, `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect`, so it always passes, as the added FIXME admits. The test also navigates to logout without waiting for the enable request or the new backup-codes screen, so it can race.

The copy test only waits for the toast, which is shown regardless of whether the clipboard write succeeded.

Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the visibility toggle button in the shared `PasswordField` makes the show/hide control unreachable by keyboard. This applies to every password field in the app, not just the 2FA modals.

This is an accessibility regression for keyboard and screen-reader users, and it is unrelated to the backup-code feature.

The calendars are filtered by the main host's destination `externalId`. A secondary host's CalDAV account never contains that URL, so the filter yields zero calendars. `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and `createEvent` returns success with a uid. A booking reference is stored for an event that was never created, and the host gets nothing in their calendar.

For a destination with no `credentialId` (legacy rows), the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `destination.externalId`. The resulting reference therefore stores no `externalCalendarId`; previously it stored `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Later updates and deletes then can't target the right calendar.

If a collective team member's destination calendar lacks a credentialId, an extra event is created in every organizer calendar of that integration type. The organizer gets duplicates and the team member gets nothing.

`console.error(message)` was removed. `message` is still computed and then unused. Failures updating calendar events are now swallowed silently and only appear as generic `success: false` results, which makes production issues hard to diagnose.

Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without credentialId

The calendar is now chosen only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, with fallback to "primary". Legacy destination calendars with a null `credentialId` used to have their `externalId` respected. They now silently get events written to the primary calendar instead of the user's configured destination calendar.

The same impossible `find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is used when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always falls through to "primary". If the event lives in a non-primary destination calendar, Google returns 404. The code resolves 404 silently, so the cancelled booking's event stays on the user's calendar.

Hangout-link patch uses a possibly undefined calendarId

`selectedCalendar` used to be guaranteed to be a string (`"primary"` fallback). It is now `undefined` whenever no destination matches the credential, and only the insert call applies `|| "primary"`. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` then gets `undefined` and fails, so the Meet link is never written into the description. The patch promise is not awaited or caught, so the failure is an unhandled rejection.

The PR states no tests were added. The regressions above (Meet crash on empty array, dead fallback lookups, dropped credentialId on references) would be caught by basic unit tests of these paths.

EventManager calls `createEvent` once per host's credential, but Office365 (and Lark in the same way) always uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, the main host's calendar. For a second host with Outlook, the request goes to `/me/calendars/<main host calendar id>/events` with the second host's token and fails. The PR's stated goal that every host with any calendar app gets the event is not met for these providers. Pick the destination matching the credential, as the Google service does.

The recurring-series deletion block now sits inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references it runs N times. Each run iterates all organizer credentials and deletes the first calendar reference of each updated booking, sending redundant API calls. It still uses only the organizer's credentials and only the first reference per booking. For collective recurring bookings, the other hosts' events are never deleted.

Rescheduling with newBookingId deletes only the first old calendar event

The update loop now handles one calendar reference per host. The old-event cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so it deletes only the first old calendar reference. For collective bookings, every other host keeps a stale event at the old time in their calendar.

Unrelated loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and changes error semantics

The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`, so dynamic group bookings lose the organizer's org data that was previously loaded. The rewrite also turns an empty or invalid `dynamicUserList` into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" and re-wraps any HttpError as 400, discarding its original status code. These behavior changes are outside the PR's scope and untested.

Before: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. After: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Video results from `createMeeting` carry a `credentialId`, which is now dropped. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. As a result, Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings for new bookings are orphaned on cancellation. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results too.

Webhook payload `destinationCalendar` changes from object to array (breaking)

`CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads (BOOKING_CREATED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, etc.). `destinationCalendar` changes from an object or null to an array. It is also inconsistent across triggers: `null` from handleNewBooking but `[]` from other paths, as the e2e test now expects. This breaks third-party webhook consumers, contradicting the PR's 'non-breaking' claim, and needs a migration note or payload compatibility shim.

updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId

The references now use `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. For calendar results these come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, which returns neither field. editLocation persists these as new booking references with null `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`. Previously both fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar`. Later cancellation or reschedule then falls into the legacy path or targets the wrong calendar.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Placeholder "refresh_token" overwrites the real refresh token in the default path

The fallback `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` also runs when sync is disabled. Office365's `refreshTokenResponseSchema` makes `refresh_token` optional, and the caller spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials. Previously, if Microsoft omitted a refresh_token, the existing one was kept. Now it is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token", and every later refresh fails permanently. Only inject the placeholder in sync mode, or don't inject it at all.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Minimum token schema strips every field except access_token

`[z.string().toString()]` is not a pattern key. `ZodString.toString()` returns "[object Object]", so both computed keys are the same literal property "[object Object]" and the second overwrites the first. The effective schema is `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}` in zod's default strip mode. In sync mode every other property is therefore dropped: expiry_date, expires_in, scope, token_type, instance_url, etc. The consequences differ per app. Zoom computes `expiry_date` from an undefined `expires_in` (NaN, stored as null), so the next `zoomTokenSchema.parse` fails. Salesforce loses `instance_url`. Google loses `expiry_date`, `scope` and `token_type`. Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record`/`.catchall` with an explicit expiry field.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key is overwritten with a `{success, data}` wrapper on every token refresh

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `safeParse` result object, not the parsed data. Before this change, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the token itself. Now `key` is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, and that object is written to `credential.key`. This happens in the default (non-sync) path too, so it affects every Google Calendar user. After the first refresh, the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor throws, and the Google Calendar integration stops working for that user. Store `key.data`, or have the helper return the data.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync path returns a raw fetch Response that callers expecting provider-specific objects can't use

In sync mode the helper returns a WHATWG `Response`. In native mode it returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns, so callers get a different type depending on the mode. Several callers break in sync mode:
- Google Calendar reads `res?.data`, which is undefined on a Response, so `token.access_token` throws. The error is swallowed and the expired token keeps being used.
- Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM read `tokenInfo.data.error`, the axios shape, and throw a TypeError.
- HubSpot treats the result as a token object (`expiresIn`, `accessToken`), computes a NaN expiry and stores the Response object as the credential key.

The helper should normalize the result, e.g. parse JSON and return a common token shape, or the callers must branch on mode.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential id passed as the Cal.com user id to the sync endpoint

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credential.id` where the helper expects `userId`. The sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>`. It will return tokens for whichever user happens to have that id, or for nobody. In the first case one user's Zoho tokens get written into another user's credential. Team credentials (userId null) are also sent to the sync endpoint, against the helper's stated intent. Pass `credential.userId` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Success is detected via `statusText === "OK"`

`statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 responses and is not guaranteed to be "OK" for a 200, so a successful refresh can be reported as a 400 error. Use `response.ok`. Also, the `!accessTokenParsed.success` branch below is dead, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure instead of returning success=false.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation, then ignores the new token

`getClient` now unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint every time the service is constructed, with no expiry check. That adds latency and rate-limit pressure on every booking. Afterwards the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `instance_url` instead of the freshly refreshed values, so the extra request achieves nothing for the current call. The URL is also hardcoded to `login.salesforce.com`, which breaks sandbox orgs. This refresh also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` while still using the sync-mode schema, which corrupts the stored key (see the schema stripping issue).

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Malformed body or bad ciphertext returns an unhandled 500

`schema.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` all throw on bad input, and nothing catches them. The caller gets a generic 500 instead of a 400 explaining what was wrong. The decrypted keys are also stored without any validation against the app's credential schema.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the new refresh/sync helpers or the webhook

The PR changes token refresh for about ten integrations and adds a credential-writing webhook, and it states that no tests were added or run. Unit tests for `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught several of the issues above: the returned wrapper object, the fields stripped by the broken schema, and the placeholder refresh_token. The same goes for `refreshOAuthTokens` (sync vs native return types) and the webhook (slug→metadata lookup).

Outbound sync request carries no authentication

Cal.com POSTs only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to the sync endpoint, with no shared secret, signature or encryption. The inbound webhook, by contrast, requires a secret and AES-encrypted keys. The self-hoster's endpoint therefore has no way to verify that the caller is Cal.com. Anyone who can reach it can enumerate user ids and obtain live third-party access tokens. Send the webhook secret or an HMAC header, and ideally encrypt the response with the shared key. Also check `response.ok` before returning.

Removed diagnostic logging of the Microsoft refresh error

The old code logged the zod error and the raw Microsoft response when parsing failed. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and the MS error body is lost. That makes Outlook token problems much harder to debug. The behavior also changed from "keep the old token and continue" to "throw".

Updating a credential via the webhook doesn't clear `invalid`

Google, Zoom and Webex set `invalid: true` on invalid_grant. When the parent app later pushes fresh keys through this webhook, only `key` is updated. The credential stays flagged invalid and is still treated as broken. Reset `invalid: false` on update.

Webex, Lark and MS Teams still require the provider-native response shape in sync mode

Webex validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` directly, which requires a scope literal, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. Lark runs it through `handleLarkError`, which expects `{code:0,data:{...}}`. MS Teams overwrites the entire stored key with the response. All three are routed to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, whose documented contract is "only the access token and expiry date". With a conforming endpoint, Webex rejects every refresh, Lark throws, and Teams loses its refresh_token. The endpoint contract is not consistent across the integrations this PR switches over.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`

The secret is compared with `!==`, which leaks timing information. If the header is sent more than once it becomes a `string[]` and never matches. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on the buffers after checking the lengths. The endpoint also accepts any HTTP method.

Zoom sends app slug "zoomvideo" instead of "zoom"

Zoom's app slug and appId is "zoom" (see `createOAuthAppCredential({ appId: "zoom" ...})` in the callback). The webhook also identifies apps by slug. The refresh call sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, the directory name, so the self-hoster's sync endpoint gets an identifier that doesn't match what it uses for the webhook. Zoom refreshes will fail or return the wrong app's tokens.

`prisma` used without being imported

The new `prisma.credential.update(...)` call references `prisma`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. At best it resolves to the dev-only `globalThis.prisma`. In production that global is not set, so this throws a ReferenceError/TypeError. Since `getClient` runs in the constructor, every Salesforce booking/CRM operation fails.

appStoreMetadata is indexed by slug, but it is keyed by app directory name

`appStoreMetadata` is generated keyed by app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`), not by slug. Looking it up with `app.slug` (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`) returns undefined, so the webhook answers 404 for most of the OAuth apps this PR targets. It only works by accident where slug equals dirName. Select `dirName` from the App row and index by that.

Given the data-loss risk if the conditions are wrong, these should be covered.

The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. All getters now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`.

`Prisma.sql` inlines nested fragments verbatim; it does not wrap them in parentheses. Several public methods return a fragment whose top level is an unparenthesized OR:
- `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` return `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)`.
- `buildFilterConditions` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` when only one filter is set.
- `getBaseConditions` returns the auth fragment bare when there are no filters.

These methods are the replacement for `findMany`, so callers must embed the fragments in their own queries. A natural pattern is `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. The result is wrong counts and leaked rows outside the requested range.

That is the exact behaviour the PR identifies as broken: it consumes SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation quota, and once the quota is full these cancels fail and rescheduled-booking reminders are still sent.

- the 100 pending-cancellation limit;
- a batch already cancelled through the `immediateDelete` path (e.g. organizer `requestReschedule` sets `cancelled=true`, then the attendee reschedules and `handleNewBooking` cancels the same batch immediately);
